1	# Structural Context
2	
3	Biotite is a Python library for computational molecular biology and structural
4	bioinformatics. The project paper describes Biotite as a toolkit for reading,
5	manipulating, analyzing, and writing biomolecular structure data, including
6	macromolecular formats used by the Protein Data Bank.
7	
8	Primary citation:
9	
10	- Patrick Kunzmann, Jochen Hamacher, Sebastian Dieterich, Markus Glaser and
11	  Andreas Hopf, "Biotite: new tools for a versatile Python bioinformatics
12	  library", BMC Bioinformatics, 2023. DOI: `10.1186/s12859-023-05345-6`.
13	
14	The relevant public workflow uses the Biotite PDBx/mmCIF interface. Its
15	structure-loading routines convert PDBx/mmCIF atom records into in-memory atom
16	arrays and can attach connectivity information when the input data and chosen
17	workflow support it.
18	
19	## PDBx/mmCIF Concepts
20	
21	PDBx/mmCIF files store atom records in the `_atom_site` category. Each row
22	describes one atomic record, including residue and atom labels, Cartesian
23	coordinates, model information, occupancy, and, when present, alternate-location
24	identifiers.
25	
26	Alternate locations describe different conformations of the same structural
27	site. Occupancy values describe how much of the crystallographic model is
28	assigned to a candidate position and are commonly used by structure software
29	when a representative set of atom records is needed.
30	
31	Choosing a representative set of records and preserving every alternate record
32	are different structural representations, and downstream interpretation depends
33	on which representation a workflow returns.
34	An ordinary bond graph records edges between atom rows; it does not by itself
35	carry a separate conformer-state annotation on each edge. Structural software
36	therefore needs the atom table, option semantics, and any reported connectivity
37	to remain mutually interpretable.
38	
39	Bond and linkage information can be represented separately from the atom rows.
40	The `_struct_conn` category records named connections between atom records, and
41	software libraries also infer standard residue-internal and polymer
42	connectivity from chemical component information and biopolymer conventions.
43	
44	Downstream workflows often interpret the returned atoms and any attached
45	connectivity together: they may segment residues, follow polymer chains, export
46	topologies, or inspect local chemical neighborhoods. Connectivity summaries such
47	as bond counts, component sizes, and isolated atoms are therefore useful
48	diagnostics for deciding whether a structure-loading result is chemically
49	plausible.

180	        Default is the first (and most times only) data block of the
181	        file.

183	        this parameter is ignored.

196	    version of this initial sequence, it will include only a subset of the

249	def get_structure(
250	    pdbx_file,
251	    model=None,
252	    data_block=None,
253	    altloc="first",
254	    extra_fields=None,
255	    use_author_fields=True,
256	    include_bonds=False,
257	):
258	    """
259	    Create an :class:`AtomArray` or :class:`AtomArrayStack` from the
260	    ``atom_site`` category in a file.
261	
262	    Parameters
263	    ----------
264	    pdbx_file : CIFFile or CIFBlock or BinaryCIFFile or BinaryCIFBlock
265	        The file object.
266	    model : int, optional
267	        If this parameter is given, the function will return an
268	        :class:`AtomArray` from the atoms corresponding to the given
269	        model number (starting at 1).
270	        Negative values are used to index models starting from the last
271	        model insted of the first model.
272	        If this parameter is omitted, an :class:`AtomArrayStack`
273	        containing all models will be returned, even if the structure
274	        contains only one model.
275	    data_block : str, optional
276	        The name of the data block.
277	        Default is the first (and most times only) data block of the
278	        file.
279	        If the data block object is passed directly to `pdbx_file`,
280	        this parameter is ignored.
281	    altloc : {'first', 'occupancy', 'all'}
282	        This parameter defines how *altloc* IDs are handled:
283	            - ``'first'`` - Use atoms that have the first *altloc* ID
284	              appearing in a residue.
285	            - ``'occupancy'`` - Use atoms that have the *altloc* ID
286	              with the highest occupancy for a residue.
287	            - ``'all'`` - Use all atoms.
288	              Note that this leads to duplicate atoms.
289	              When this option is chosen, the ``altloc_id`` annotation
290	              array is added to the returned structure.
291	    extra_fields : list of str, optional
292	        The strings in the list are entry names, that are
293	        additionally added as annotation arrays.
294	        The annotation category name will be the same as the PDBx
295	        subcategory name.
296	        The array type is always `str`.
297	        An exception are the special field identifiers:
298	        ``'atom_id'``, ``'b_factor'``, ``'occupancy'`` and ``'charge'``.
299	        These will convert the fitting subcategory into an
300	        annotation array with reasonable type.
301	    use_author_fields : bool, optional
302	        Some fields can be read from two alternative sources,
303	        for example both, ``label_seq_id`` and ``auth_seq_id`` describe
304	        the ID of the residue.
305	        While, the ``label_xxx`` fields can be used as official pointers
306	        to other categories in the file, the ``auth_xxx``
307	        fields are set by the author(s) of the structure and are
308	        consistent with the corresponding values in PDB files.
309	        If `use_author_fields` is true, the annotation arrays will be
310	        read from the ``auth_xxx`` fields (if applicable),
311	        otherwise from the the ``label_xxx`` fields.
312	        If the requested field is not available, the respective other
313	        field is taken as fallback.
314	    include_bonds : bool, optional
315	        If set to true, a :class:`BondList` will be created for the
316	        resulting :class:`AtomArray` containing the bond information
317	        from the file.
318	        Inter-residue bonds, will be read from the ``struct_conn``
319	        category.
320	        Intra-residue bonds will be read from the ``chem_comp_bond``, if
321	        available, otherwise they will be derived from the Chemical
322	        Component Dictionary.
323	
324	    Returns
325	    -------
326	    array : AtomArray or AtomArrayStack
327	        The return type depends on the `model` parameter.
328	
329	    Examples
330	    --------
331	
332	    >>> import os.path
333	    >>> file = CIFFile.read(os.path.join(path_to_structures, "1l2y.cif"))
334	    >>> arr = get_structure(file, model=1)
335	    >>> print(len(arr))
336	    304
337	    """
338	    block = _get_block(pdbx_file, data_block)
339	
340	    extra_fields = set() if extra_fields is None else set(extra_fields)
341	
342	    atom_site = block.get("atom_site")
343	    if atom_site is None:
344	        raise InvalidFileError("Missing 'atom_site' category in file")
345	
346	    models = atom_site["pdbx_PDB_model_num"].as_array(np.int32)
347	    model_count = len(np.unique(models))
348	    atom_count = len(models)
349	
350	    if model is None:
351	        # For a stack, the annotations are derived from the first model
352	        model_atom_site = _filter_model(atom_site, 1)
353	        # Any field of the category would work here to get the length
354	        model_length = model_atom_site.row_count
355	        atoms = AtomArrayStack(model_count, model_length)
356	
357	        # Check if each model has the same amount of atoms
358	        # If not, raise exception
359	        if model_length * model_count != atom_count:
360	            raise InvalidFileError(
361	                "The models in the file have unequal "
362	                "amount of atoms, give an explicit model "
363	                "instead"
364	            )
365	
366	        atoms.coord[:, :, 0] = (
367	            atom_site["Cartn_x"]
368	            .as_array(np.float32)
369	            .reshape((model_count, model_length))
370	        )
371	        atoms.coord[:, :, 1] = (
372	            atom_site["Cartn_y"]
373	            .as_array(np.float32)
374	            .reshape((model_count, model_length))
375	        )
376	        atoms.coord[:, :, 2] = (
377	            atom_site["Cartn_z"]
378	            .as_array(np.float32)
379	            .reshape((model_count, model_length))
380	        )
381	
382	        box = _get_box(block)
383	        if box is not None:
384	            # Duplicate same box for each model
385	            atoms.box = np.repeat(box[np.newaxis, ...], model_count, axis=0)
386	
387	    else:
388	        if model == 0:
389	            raise ValueError("The model index must not be 0")
390	        # Negative models mean model indexing starting from last model
391	        model = model_count + model + 1 if model < 0 else model
392	        if model > model_count:
393	            raise ValueError(
394	                f"The file has {model_count} models, "
395	                f"the given model {model} does not exist"
396	            )
397	
398	        model_atom_site = _filter_model(atom_site, model)
399	        # Any field of the category would work here to get the length
400	        model_length = model_atom_site.row_count
401	        atoms = AtomArray(model_length)
402	
403	        atoms.coord[:, 0] = model_atom_site["Cartn_x"].as_array(np.float32)
404	        atoms.coord[:, 1] = model_atom_site["Cartn_y"].as_array(np.float32)
405	        atoms.coord[:, 2] = model_atom_site["Cartn_z"].as_array(np.float32)
406	
407	        atoms.box = _get_box(block)
408	
409	    # The below part is the same for both, AtomArray and AtomArrayStack
410	    _fill_annotations(atoms, model_atom_site, extra_fields, use_author_fields)
411	    if include_bonds:
412	        if "chem_comp_bond" in block:
413	            try:
414	                custom_bond_dict = _parse_intra_residue_bonds(block["chem_comp_bond"])
415	            except KeyError:
416	                warnings.warn(
417	                    "The 'chem_comp_bond' category has missing columns, "
418	                    "falling back to using Chemical Component Dictionary",
419	                    UserWarning,
420	                )
421	                custom_bond_dict = None
422	            bonds = connect_via_residue_names(atoms, custom_bond_dict=custom_bond_dict)
423	        else:
424	            bonds = connect_via_residue_names(atoms)
425	        if "struct_conn" in block:
426	            bonds = bonds.merge(
427	                _parse_inter_residue_bonds(model_atom_site, block["struct_conn"])
428	            )
429	        atoms.bonds = bonds
430	    atoms = _filter_altloc(atoms, model_atom_site, altloc)
431	
432	    return atoms

590	def _parse_inter_residue_bonds(atom_site, struct_conn):
591	    """
592	    Create inter-residue bonds by parsing the ``struct_conn`` category.
593	    The atom indices of each bond are found by matching the bond labels
594	    to the ``atom_site`` category.
595	    """
596	    # Identity symmetry operation
597	    IDENTITY = "1_555"
598	    # Columns in 'atom_site' that should be matched by 'struct_conn'
599	    COLUMNS = [
600	        "label_asym_id",
601	        "label_comp_id",
602	        "label_seq_id",
603	        "label_atom_id",
604	        "label_alt_id",
605	        "auth_asym_id",
606	        "auth_comp_id",
607	        "auth_seq_id",
608	        "pdbx_PDB_ins_code",
609	    ]
610	
611	    covale_mask = np.isin(
612	        struct_conn["conn_type_id"].as_array(str),
613	        list(PDBX_BOND_TYPE_ID_TO_TYPE.keys()),
614	    )
615	    if "ptnr1_symmetry" in struct_conn:
616	        covale_mask &= struct_conn["ptnr1_symmetry"].as_array(str, IDENTITY) == IDENTITY
617	    if "ptnr2_symmetry" in struct_conn:
618	        covale_mask &= struct_conn["ptnr2_symmetry"].as_array(str, IDENTITY) == IDENTITY
619	
620	    atom_indices = [None] * 2
621	    for i in range(2):
622	        reference_arrays = []
623	        query_arrays = []
624	        for col_name in COLUMNS:
625	            struct_conn_col_name = _get_struct_conn_col_name(col_name, i + 1)
626	            if col_name not in atom_site or struct_conn_col_name not in struct_conn:
627	                continue
628	            # Ensure both arrays have the same dtype to allow comparison
629	            reference = atom_site[col_name].as_array()
630	            dtype = reference.dtype
631	            query = struct_conn[struct_conn_col_name].as_array(dtype)
632	            if np.issubdtype(reference.dtype, str):
633	                # The mask value is not necessarily consistent
634	                # between query and reference
635	                # -> make it consistent
636	                reference[reference == "?"] = "."
637	                query[query == "?"] = "."
638	            reference_arrays.append(reference)
639	            query_arrays.append(query[covale_mask])
640	        # Match the combination of 'label_asym_id', 'label_comp_id', etc.
641	        # in 'atom_site' and 'struct_conn'
642	        atom_indices[i] = _find_matches(query_arrays, reference_arrays)
643	    atoms_indices_1 = atom_indices[0]
644	    atoms_indices_2 = atom_indices[1]
645	
646	    # Some bonds in 'struct_conn' may not be found in 'atom_site'
647	    # This is okay,
648	    # as 'atom_site' might already be reduced to a single model
649	    mapping_exists_mask = (atoms_indices_1 != -1) & (atoms_indices_2 != -1)
650	    atoms_indices_1 = atoms_indices_1[mapping_exists_mask]
651	    atoms_indices_2 = atoms_indices_2[mapping_exists_mask]
652	
653	    bond_type_id = struct_conn["conn_type_id"].as_array()
654	    # Consecutively apply the same masks as applied to the atom indices
655	    # Logical combination does not work here,
656	    # as the second mask was created based on already filtered data
657	    bond_type_id = bond_type_id[covale_mask][mapping_exists_mask]
658	    # The type ID is always present in the dictionary,
659	    # as it was used to filter the applicable bonds
660	    bond_types = [PDBX_BOND_TYPE_ID_TO_TYPE[type_id] for type_id in bond_type_id]
661	
662	    return BondList(
663	        atom_site.row_count,
664	        np.stack([atoms_indices_1, atoms_indices_2, bond_types], axis=-1),
665	    )
666

668	def _find_matches(query_arrays, reference_arrays):
669	    """
670	    For each index in the `query_arrays` find the indices in the
671	    `reference_arrays` where all query values match the reference counterpart.
672	    If no match is found for a query, the corresponding index is -1.
673	    """
674	    if (
675	        query_arrays[0].shape[0] * reference_arrays[0].shape[0]
676	        <= FIND_MATCHES_SWITCH_THRESHOLD
677	    ):
678	        match_indices = _find_matches_by_dense_array(query_arrays, reference_arrays)
679	    else:
680	        match_indices = _find_matches_by_dict(query_arrays, reference_arrays)
681	    return match_indices
